extracted.intended_audience: NIH/NIAID grant reviewers, diagnostics developers, translational researchers in point-of-care HIV diagnostics
extracted.subtask_description: Development, integration, and validation of a cartridge-based point-of-care HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody (4th generation) combo assay intended to match laboratory 4th gen Ag/Ab combo performance while meeting FDA/CLIA requirements for non-lab use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II Aim 1 performance equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1 milestone is an HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody detection assay with performance equivalent to FDA-approved laboratory 4th gen Ag/Ab combo assays for the MBio early/acute sample collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent performance is to be demonstrated against a defined early/acute sample collection (seroconversion/performance panels, anti-HIV-2 panels, and unique acute samples). Use the same NIBSC p24 reference standard and comparative testing against commercial 4th gen assays (e.g., Abbott ARCHITECT, Bio-Rad GS) as benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartridge integration and CLIA-waiver readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2 milestone: a portable, integrated system (Cartridge, Rack, Reader, Software) that delivers an automated HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab combo result and incorporates heat-stable assay reagents into the cartridge, meeting FDA CLIA waiver guidance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design goals include minimal user steps, small sample (fingerstick), error tolerance, on-cartridge lyophilization of reagents, potential on-cartridge wash mechanism without user intervention, and delivery of an integrated system to clinical collaborators for usability testing and pre-IDE preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation sample set size and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 3 milestone: validate the system using a panel of 200 HIV-positive specimens (including 20 acute infection samples: RNA+ / Ab-) and 200 HIV-negative samples for specificity testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive panel must include acute, early seroconversion (Western blot indeterminate), seropositive HIV-1 and HIV-2 samples. Validation dataset should demonstrate performance equivalent to FDA-approved laboratory 4th gen assays and support an IDE meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-market field evaluation dataset and usability capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 4 milestone: place systems in intended use settings, capture operational and usability feedback, and generate a preliminary dataset on capillary whole blood samples from ~100 study participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the field evaluation to inform design lock and produce a system design and dataset suitable for an FDA IDE meeting prior to clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical sensitivity (limit of detection) standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the WHO International Standard HIV-1 p24 reagent (NIBSC code: 90/636) expressed in IU/mL as the basis for analytical sensitivity comparisons; diagnostic antigen assays are expected to have analytical sensitivity of 2 IU/mL or better (per referenced European Commission standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine LLOD via serial dilutions of the NIBSC standard; report LLOD in IU/mL. Compare assay LLOD to commercial assays (e.g., ARCHITECT 1.24 IU/mL) and document intra-experiment variability (error bars, %CV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutoff determination methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Define positive assay cutoff values using mean + (5 x standard deviation) from a panel of negative samples (e.g., 40 HIV-negative serum samples) or no-spike normal serum controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently apply the cutoff computation method (mean + 5 SD) across comparative assays to enable fair sensitivity/specificity comparisons; document the negative-sample set composition and replicate counts used to compute mean and SD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay reproducibility metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report assay variability including %CV at the limits of detection, intra-spot %CV, and lot-to-lot reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use replicate measurements (e.g., triplicates, 5+ replicates for controls) to calculate %CV at LLOD and report error bars (±1 stdev). Include metrics for spot morphology and intra-spot variability as part of antibody print optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol simplicity and user-interaction limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce assay complexity such that total assay time ≤ 30 minutes and the number of user interactions/steps is no more than two requiring user involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to achieve a one-step or two-step protocol (e.g., sample + reagent incubation then magnetic wash/read) compatible with fingerstick whole blood. If necessary, redesign cartridge for automated washing and reagent reconstitution to meet CLIA waiver simplicity criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample volume and specimen types
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay must operate on limited sample volumes appropriate for fingerstick whole blood (examples in text: 21 µL, 25 µL) and be validated on capillary whole blood as well as plasma/serum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate equivalent performance on whole blood samples (reported experiment: N=59 whole blood samples, N=34 HIV-positive, N=25 negative) and show clear separation of positive/negative signal distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I comparative sensitivity milestone (Specific Aim 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I milestone: quantitatively compare MBio assays to gold-standard methods and detect 80% of HIV-1 positive samples not detected with the current market-leading FDA-approved HIV-1/2 rapid test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform head-to-head testing against rapid tests and EIAs (OraQuick, Uni-Gold, PerkinElmer ELISA, GS HIV-1/2 Combo) using the same recent-infection panel; report per-sample S/CO values and compute sensitivity percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking against named commercial assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark MBio assay results versus specific commercial systems (Abbott ARCHITECT, Bio-Rad GS HIV Combo, PerkinElmer HIV p24 ELISA, VIDAS assays, lateral flow Determine®) and use product-insert or in-house run data for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identical sample panels and follow product-insert protocols for the comparator assays; present tabulated per-sample results and aggregated sensitivity/specificity comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virus disruption additive compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate a virus disruption sample additive (VDSA) to increase detectable p24 without compromising antibody detection in the combined Ag/Ab assay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate VDSA (ionic detergents, salts, chelators per proposal) and test five acute samples; demonstrate improved p24 S/CO while showing no adverse effect on serology signals. Keep formulation trade secrets if proprietary, but validate compatibility experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody and antigen selection and supply stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Select final monoclonal/polyclonal antibody pairs and HIV-1/HIV-2 antigens with attention to performance, availability, and long-term supply agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen candidate mAbs as capture/detect agents, evaluate supply chain (cGMP suppliers), consider antigenic peptides to improve specificity, and include supply agreements as part of productization readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay optimization practices and experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a Design of Experiments (DOE) approach for optimizing antibody print buffers, dye labeling, and other assay parameters; perform titrations (three-point for NIBSC standard) and iterative screening with defined negative panels (e.g., 8-member HA panel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize detect-antigen/antibody concentration to avoid hook effects and saturation; consider switching to brighter fluorophores (SLP3 vs A647) based on S/N and detectability assessments; document decision criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reactivity and non-specific binding assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate non-specific binding between candidate capture antigens and anti-p24 detect mAb and vice versa to minimize cross-reactivity and false signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experiments to detect capture->detect cross-reactivity, perform HA blocking strategies, and include HA-containing negative samples in specificity testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing cost and cartridge design constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Design disposable cartridges to be assembled from injection-molded plastics within established manufacturing tolerances and target assembly costs comparable to existing lateral flow rapid tests (< $1 per piece manufactured cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cartridge feature sizes are manufacturable, incorporate molded waveguide and reagent stabilization (heat-stable, lyophilized reagents), and plan for scale-up reproducibility and cost targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaging/readout and throughput metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader imaging time (example: ~30 seconds read), magnetic focusing and image analysis-based bead counting, and signal acquisition must provide reliable quantitative outputs with acceptable throughput.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use custom image analysis to count magnetic bead–fluorescent bead complexes, report signal-to-noise, and ensure imaging/read times are compatible with POC workflows; validate software quantitation and QC procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and pre-market data package objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate a system design and validation dataset adequate for an FDA investigational device exemption (IDE) meeting, position for PMA clinical trials and subsequent CLIA waiver evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture field usability/operational data, show analytical and clinical performance equivalent to laboratory standards, document manufacturing controls and reagent supply, and prepare for pre-IDE discussions with FDA.
